items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was also a great hamburger stand on the other side of the Club owned by a fellow named Jesse Wynn. Jesse made hamburgers so tasty that they almost melted in your mouth.

ctx.x: to Connie's was in this alley. What Bobby had done was to tell the driver of the taxi to wait a minute for him and he had gone in the alley and come out on 7th Avenue. I did the same thing out of curiosity, came out on 7th Avenue and walked around to the Rhythm Club. There was Bobby as unconcerned as if nothing had happened. He told me that he had not intended to pay the taxi and that was a trick he had pulled before. I didn't like it but couldn't do anything about it.

There was a well-known restaurant next door to the Club called Tabbs that never closed and it was very practical for entertainers and musicians who worked late and wanted to have some food before they went to sleep. There was also a great hamburger stand on the other side of the Club owned by a fellow named Jesse Wynn. Jesse made hamburgers so tasty that they almost melted in your mouth.

Tabbs had the best hominy grits, sausages and eggs with hot biscuits and butter oozing from them, that you ever stuck a tooth in. And thats what I decided to have after I left Bobby to feed some of the juice that I had drunk at his uncle's place. Bobby Starke and I became very good friends.
